title: Econ 101 lecture 4 notes
subject: Economics
text:
lecture 4 - supply & demand (prof said this is on the midterm!!)

demand = how much ppl want to buy at each price. law of demand: price up -> qty demanded down (other things equal / ceteris paribus)

demand curve slopes DOWN. movement along curve = price change. SHIFT of curve = something else changes (income, tastes, price of substitutes, expectations)

normal goods: income up -> demand up. inferior goods: income up -> demand DOWN (ex: instant noodles?? he said bus tickets)

supply = how much firms want to sell. law of supply: price up -> qty supplied up. curve slopes UP

supply shifts: input costs, technology, number of sellers, taxes/subsidies

equilibrium = where curves cross. P* and Q*. if price above P* -> surplus -> price falls. below -> shortage -> price rises

!! dont mix up 'change in demand' (shift) vs 'change in quantity demanded' (movement) - classic exam trap

example from class: coffee frost in brazil -> supply shifts left -> price up, qty down

price ceiling (max price, e.g. rent control) below eq -> shortage. price floor (min wage) above eq -> surplus
